sections.heading: 1. Project information
sections.guidance: Project name, number, address, client, appointment, key dates. Mirror the project record — this section is the document's identity page.

sections.heading: 2. Roles, responsibilities and authorities
sections.guidance: Information management roles per ISO 19650-2 §5.1: appointing party, lead appointed party, task teams. Include a responsibility summary (who produces, who checks, who accepts).

sections.heading: 3. Information delivery strategy
sections.guidance: Objectives for information delivery, key decision points, alignment with the client's EIR. State the federation strategy at a high level.

sections.heading: 4. Federation strategy and model breakdown
sections.guidance: How models are split (by discipline, zone, level), federation frequency, coordination process and clash workflow.

sections.heading: 5. CDE and workflow
sections.guidance: The common data environment, container states (WIP → Shared → Published → Archived), transitions, approval gates and who authorises them.

sections.heading: 6. Container naming and standards
sections.guidance: The naming convention every information container must follow (fields, separators, codes). This section binds to Sentinel's naming ruleset in a later release.

sections.heading: 7. Level of information need (LOIN)
sections.guidance: What geometric/alphanumeric information is required per deliverable and milestone. Reference the LOIN tables from the EIR.

sections.heading: 8. Methods and procedures
sections.guidance: Modelling methods, shared coordinates, units, classification system, QA checks before sharing.

sections.heading: 9. Software and versions
sections.guidance: Authoring and checking tools with exact versions, exchange formats (IFC MVDs), and upgrade policy for the appointment.

sections.heading: 10. Quality assurance and model checking
sections.guidance: Checks run before each state transition (naming, clash, data completeness), who runs them, acceptance criteria.
